notes: Fixes both root causes: a reusable caller with expanded children now takes its children's aggregated status (so it stays Cancelling until the runner acknowledges, at any depth), and `cancelRun` re-emits a run that settled without any job update so blocked concurrency waiters wake. Minor fragility: `cancelOneJob` returns the caller as cancelled even when aggregation leaves it unchanged, and it relies on descendants being cancelled first. Tests cover nested callers through runner ack and force-cancel of an already-stuck run, though the waiter wake-up is checked via a mocked emitter plus a separate `checkRunConcurrency` call.

Fixes both root causes. A reusable caller with expanded children now takes its status from those children, so it stays cancelling until the runner acknowledges, at any nesting depth. A cancel or force-cancel that settles a run without updating any job now re-emits the run so its concurrency waiters start. Small concerns: the caller is reported as cancelled even when its aggregated status is unchanged or non-cancelled, and the emit is best-effort and only logs failures. Model and service tests are focused and cover both scenarios well.

Clean, consistent symlink support for both zip and squashfs: links are skipped unless --links is set, a notice names the flag, links get the .rclonelink suffix, size is the target length, squashfs Open handles range/seek, and List and NewObject agree. However, hostile-archive safety relies entirely on the local backend rather than dropping members beneath a symlink, a symlink can collide with a regular 'x.rclonelink' member, and the escape test only covers the case where the outside target directory does not exist.

Implements --links gating with a notice naming the flag, the .rclonelink naming, target-length size and range-aware reads for both zip and squashfs, keeps List and NewObject in agreement, and leaves plain *.rclonelink members as regular files; minor gaps are possible duplicate names when an archive has both `x` (symlink) and `x.rclonelink`, a squashfs root pointing directly at a link, relying on the local backend to block the escape, and no zip tests for range reads or literal .rclonelink members.

The SNMP fix itself is sound: `Close()` is added to the interface, the connection is closed when the top-level fields or a table fail, `Reconnect` clears the USM engine ID, boots and time only when the connection is closed, and `Get`/`Walk` reconnect first, with focused tests for each. However, the patch also rewrites MIB path loading in `mib_loader.go` (custom `AppendFS` filesystem, silently skipping unreadable paths), which changes behaviour the issue never asked for and would block merging. Minor issues: the `gs.Close()` errors are ignored, and a user-configured engine ID is dropped after the first reconnect.

The SNMP fix itself is correct: it adds Close() to the Connection interface, has Get/Walk reconnect first, clears USM engine ID/boots/time only when reconnecting a closed connection, and closes the connection on gather errors with focused tests. However, the patch also rewrites unrelated MIB path loading in mib_loader.go (custom fs, silently skipping unreadable paths) and adds a test for it, which is a serious scope violation and a behavior risk; the return value of gs.Close() is also ignored in snmp.go.

Fixes the root cause: Close() no longer calls File(), which leaked a dup'd fd and unlinked the bogus fd name, and reuseUnixSocket now closes its dup'd file. Close() is serialized with listen under unixSocketsMu so close/relisten races are safe, a CAS flag makes a second Close return net.ErrClosed without touching the refcount, and the real path from Addr() is unlinked except for Linux abstract sockets, which are now also skipped at listen time. Tests are thorough and cover the immediate close plus unlink, reference counting, double close, concurrent relisten for both unix and unixgram, and abstract sockets, though the abstract-socket test writes a sentinel file into the package directory and the local-variable name in listen.go shadows the new helper.

Fixes the root cause: Close no longer leaks a dup'd fd via File(), unlinks the real path from Addr() rather than the bogus file name, and reuse now closes its dup'd file. It adds an idempotent close returning net.ErrClosed, serializes close against listen under the mutex, and protects abstract sockets on both listen and close; it does not fix the pre-existing case where the map can still point at a closed wrapper while other holders remain.
